rachel: quick one0019 — i'm returning from parental leave in mid-dec and heard there's a PTO cutoff on Dec 31. how do we handle carryover and accruals for returners?

jess (People Ops): welcome back early! good Q. short version: we restore accrued balance for the return year per policy and make special accommodations for LOA returners around the cutoff. long: if the LOA covered the cutoff period, we evaluate case-by-case. for paid parental leave we typically credit the prorated accruals for the active months; for unpaid leave accruals pause. we also accept medical/leave paperwork to request carryover exceptions.

tom (eng): do managers need to pre-approve these carryovers before people-ops? or can we submit after the return?

jess (People Ops): process: manager + employee submit a joint request in the portal within 30 days of return. people-ops then reviews and finalizes. if someone returns after Jan 31 due to approved extended leave, we still accept medical exceptions if documentation is provided.

devon: what's the math for prorating when someone returns mid-month? is it days-based or month-based?

jess (People Ops): days-based. example we use in the portal: monthly accrual * (days worked in month / total days in month). we round to nearest half-hour for PTO. i'll paste the calc formula in the portal sample.

rachel: if we approve an exception to carry over >40h, does that count as taxable income or anything special?

jess (People Ops): carryover itself is not taxable. payout of unused PTO (if applicable per local law) may be taxable and depends on jurisdiction. people-ops/finance will flag any payout scenarios and advise. exceptions to carryover don't trigger automatic payouts; they're simply reconciliation of balance.

tom (eng): one practical ask 11 managers need a checklist for return-to-work PTO handling. can people-ops provide a short template so we don't miss docs?

jess (People Ops): yes. quick manager checklist we recommend: 
1) confirm return date and LOA type in HR portal
2) employee + manager submit carryover/adjustment request (within 30 days of return)
3) attach LOA paperwork if unpaid or medical docs if applicable
4) outline proposed carryover hours and any coverage notes
5) people-ops reviews and finalizes

people-ops-bot: Reminder: "Return-from-LOA carryover requests: submit within 30 days of return. Jan 31 cutoff exceptions for medical leave accepted with documentation." <https://hr.redwood.com/loa-return>

devon: thanks. also if someone wants to use prorated accrual immediately on their first day back (for travel), is that OK?

jess (People Ops): yes they can request immediate PTO use but manager approval required. if coverage is tight, managers can deny or ask for a partial schedule. encourage folks to coordinate at least 48 hours in advance where possible.

rachel: appreciate it. can you DM me the sample request template?

jess (People Ops): will do. i'll also upload the manager checklist and calc examples to the HR docs and post in #announcements by EOD.

people-ops-bot: Policy snippet: "LOA return PTO: days-based prorate. Submit adjustments within 30 days; medical exceptions accepted after Jan 31 if documented."
